answer: Sparse-Thread Delegation Graph. Each agent must name two distinct sponsors; an agent counts as real only when its sponsors sit in separate clusters whose combined neighbourhoods fail to overlap beyond a fixed threshold. A ripple of trust then propagates only through disjoint paths, so forged agents cannot cluster. The rule: any identity whose sponsor paths merge within one hop is downweighted to zero, and a sudden gale of new names from one neighbourhood flags the whole region.
